content: Screening for lung cancer is recommended exclusively for adults who are considered to be at high risk for developing the disease. It is important to understand the fundamental aspects of lung cancer, including its symptoms, risk factors, available screening methods, and treatment options. To reduce the risk of lung cancer, individuals should avoid exposure to tobacco smoke and ensure their homes are tested for radon, a known carcinogen. The most recent federal data provides updated statistics on the incidence of lung cancer cases and related mortality rates. Lung cancer can develop in individuals who have never smoked, and this may be attributed to other risk factors such as environmental exposures or genetic predispositions. For individuals living with lung cancer, there are various tips and resources available to help manage the disease and improve quality of life. Communities play a vital role in supporting efforts to reduce lung cancer risk by promoting awareness, providing resources, and encouraging preventive measures.
